title: Test two machine light curtains over their whole field with test rods and tag out the one that fails
instruction: Test each machine's light curtain over its whole protective field with its test rod, watching the lamp, and put the DO NOT USE tag in the holder of any machine whose curtain fails.
context: Operators and maintenance workers prove a machine's safety light curtain before the shift with the supplied test rod (30 mm for a hand-protection curtain): as in the SICK deTec4 operating instructions (8021645, section 4.5.1) the rod is moved slowly through the whole protected area and along its edges while the receiver's lamp must stay red throughout; a curtain that shows green anywhere is taken out of service with a tag on the machine. Done by general maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071, about 1.5 million US workers), industrial machinery mechanics (49-9041, about 400,000) and packaging and filling machine operators (51-9111); a daily or per-shift check under IEC 61496-2 and the machine's own instructions. Here two benchtop machines stand side by side, one curtain has a dead beam (any of its 8) and the other is sound; which one and which beam change every trial.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Two identical safety light curtains, each a pair of 40 x 40 mm yellow housings 230 mm tall on 90 x 90 mm foot plates, protected height 150 mm (52 to 202 mm above the table), 400 mm between the lenses; field centres at (0.44, 0.38) and (0.44, -0.38), the field plane facing the robot (x = 0.44). Each has 8 beams 20 mm apart with 10 mm lenses (30 mm resolution) and a lamp on the receiver's top cap: green while clear, red while a beam is interrupted. Each machine has a 30 mm test rod (300 mm, 110 g, aluminium tube with yellow and black bands) resting on two saddles in front of its field, tip 5 cm short of the plane, and an empty tag holder (a slot 8 mm wide, 90 mm long) 15 cm in front of the plane beside the field. A red 76 x 127 x 5 mm DO NOT USE tag stands in a rack at (0.26, 0). One receiver has a dead beam channel (one of the 8, at 57 + 20k mm above the table); which machine and which channel are drawn at random every trial. The dead beam is seen only through the lamp: it stays green where the 30 mm rod covers only that beam (axis within 9.5 mm of it) and is red elsewhere in the field. The buildable real fixture is in REAL_FIXTURE.md: 8 TSAL6200 emitters at 38 kHz, 8 TSSP4038 receivers behind 10 mm lenses, one 2-pin link per channel into an LM339 wired-OR, a 74HC14 red/green lamp, 5 V only.
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, judged from the video. (1) Left field covered: each curtain's field is a grid of 3 lanes (along the sender post's edge, the middle, along the receiver post's edge; rod axis within 25 mm of -150, 0, +150 mm from the field's middle) by 15 cells of 10 mm of rod-axis height (52-202 mm); a cell is crossed when, at a 20 Hz step, a rod is in the field (axis within 15 degrees of the normal, tip 4 cm past the plane, between the posts, middle in front) with its axis in the lane and the cell; all 45 cells must be crossed, and each lane must be swept in one continuous run of at least 3 s at no more than 50 mm/s along the lane (150 mm / 3 s, timed with a stopwatch on the video), so a fast lane does not count even if it hit every cell. (2) The same for the right field. (3) The tag stands in the holder of the machine whose curtain missed the rod (lamp not red somewhere in its covered field; lower edge within 12 mm along the slot, 4 mm across, upright within 6 degrees), put there after that curtain's whole grid was covered, none in the other. (4) With steps 1 to 3, both rods out of both fields and every gripper at least 3 cm from the tag and the rods. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once all four steps have held together, without a break, for 1 s with the rods and the tag within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where they were when that second began; step points stop at 0.8. 0 overall if a rod or the tag is off the table.
reset_notes: Put each rod on its saddles and the tag in the rack; stand the tag holders empty. A coin flip chooses which bench test fixture has a channel open and a d8 which channel (CH0 = 57 mm, CH1 = 77 mm, ... CH7 = 197 mm): take that channel's two-pin link out on that receiver board and fit all eight links on the other. Check each by hand with the rod: the sound lamp stays red all the way up, the faulty one goes green near that channel's height. Full BOM, wiring and reset: REAL_FIXTURE.md.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control; curtains, holders, saddles, rack are fixtures. Lamp (declared effect): red/green discs on the receiver cap, red while a rod covers a whole 10 mm lens (0.5 mm slack). Fault draw random; real trial: fixture in REAL_FIXTURE.md (TSAL6200/TSSP4038, one link per channel, LM339 OR, 74HC14 lamp). Tag: 5 mm rigid sign. Rod 110 g. A lane counts only at <=50 mm/s (>=3 s/150 mm), the SICK deTec4 8021645 section 4.5.1 rate; the real trial times it on video.
scores: Dream-1 run (1,200 steps): 0.0 (both arms hovered near the rods, no rod lifted, no cell crossed, tag not moved); demo: 1.0 at step 954 with the right machine faulty and step 955 with the left one (45/45 cells and 3/3 lanes on both curtains, success at 47.2 s)
